The diagram

This is the SCON block lifted out of electrical schematic ES0366J, Service Manual page 229. Read it as two rows: the wire circuit name runs vertically above each pin, and the SCON’s own internal function name is printed below it, inside the dashed module outline.

Two names per pin, and they are not the same thing

Take J121-10. The wire is stamped S137PLL-RD/WH; the function under the pin reads P38. S137PLL is what is printed on the wire in the harness — S for safety, 137 for the circuit number, PLL for the device. P38 is what the SCON calls that output internally. When you are chasing a wire you want the first one; when you are reading a fault code you want the second.

The prefix tells you what kind of circuit it is

C control · D data · E engine · G gauges · N neutral · P power · R relay output · S safety · V valve. The number after it is the circuit number, and the same number can appear under two different prefixes — S12SB and a V12 valve wire are unrelated. Match the whole designator, never just the number. SM p.192

J122 — black 12-pin

Module supply, the safety copies of the boom angle signals, the axle and boom stowed switches, and the rest of the switched power legs — including the one that holds the engine running.

The six switched safety power outputs

This is what the SCON actually does. It takes power in, watches the safety inputs, and drops one or more of these six legs when something does not check out. Every one of them appears on a pin above.

OutputFeedsOn which pinWire
P_38PropelJ121-10S137PLL – RD/WH
P_39Turntable rotateJ121-11S139TRF – WH/RD
P_10Primary boom extendJ121-08S59CNK – GR/WH
P_11 + P_30Primary/secondary up; secondary extend and downJ122-08S140ENL – OR/RD
P_9BIgnition and fuelJ122-10P58LS – RD/BK
P_7RFoot switch / TCON E-stop powerJ121-09, J122-11S56PRV – RD
A running engine tells you something

P_9B is ignition and fuel, and the fault matrix shows Loss of CAN switches off all six legs including P_9B. So on a machine whose engine runs and keeps running, the SCON is powered, grounded, talking on CAN, and driving its outputs. A “SCON CAN no response” message on the display, on a machine that still runs, is far more likely to be latched history than a live condition.

The SCON fault matrix

Read left to right: the fault on the left, and OFF in each column the SCON switches off. This is the table that tells you why a function is dead without any wiring at all.

Three rows worth memorising
  • Primary Boom angle (crosscheck) drops P_38, P_39, P_10, P_11, P_30 — a bad primary boom angle signal kills propel and rotate, not just boom-up.
  • Loss of CAN drops all six, P_9B included, so the engine stops.
  • LSS1RS disconnected (SCON pin #2) and Platform Overload (SCON pin #1) name the pins directly — those are J121-2 and J121-1 in the table above.

Where to probe, and what you should see

Back-probe from the wire side with the connector mated. Do not spread the sockets.

  1. Supply. J122-1, P21DCON-WH to chassis ground — battery voltage with the key on and the E-stops out. This circuit leaves TCON J12-2 and feeds the DCON as well, so losing it takes out both modules at once.
  2. Ground. J121-12, GNDSCON-BR to chassis — near zero ohms. Several fault-table entries for the tilt sensors say nothing more than “check that SCON is grounded” before they say “replace SCON”, which tells you how often this is the actual fault.
  3. CAN. J121-6 is CAN High (yellow), J121-7 is CAN Low (green). A healthy 2-wire CAN bus reads roughly 60 ohms across the pair with the system powered down, and both lines sit near 2.5 V at rest with power on. general CAN practice, not a Genie spec
  4. Outputs. Check the six legs in the table above against the fault matrix. If the leg is dead and the matrix says a fault should drop it, the SCON is doing its job — go fix the input, not the module.
Before you replace one

“If the Safety Controller (SCON) has been replaced, the entire machine must be calibrated in a specific order.” That is a full machine calibration, not a quick sensor reset, and the manual carries a tip-over warning against skipping it. SM p.154

And never jumper a SCON output to get a function back. Those six legs are the machine’s entire safety envelope.

Part number and where it lives

  • 1258463GT — MODULE, SCON, PROGRAMMED, from SN 1712. This machine is Z13513-1861, so this is the one.
  • 139647-SGT — MODULE, SCON, V2.00, SERVICE, to SN 1711. Not this machine.
  • Both carry the same note: machine needs to be recalibrated after installing a new module.
  • It is item 22 on parts figure 304.1, Turntable Components — Hydraulic Tank Side.
